title: Feature Absorption as a Safety Probe Failure Mode

original_idea.body:
# Feature Absorption as a Safety Probe Failure Mode

**Problem:** Linear probes for safety concepts are trained on residual-stream activations, but SAE feature absorption silently absorbs a feature direction so the intended latent fails to fire, creating probe blind spots.

**Direction:** Using a pre-trained open SAE (Gemma-2-2B via SAELens) and a safety-relevant feature, construct absorbing-context prompts and measure whether a downstream probe's recall drops there.

**Why it matters:** Absorption blind spots mean monitoring probes fail in adversary-engineerable contexts. No-training study.

**Relevant context:** Chanin et al. (arXiv 2409.14507); SAELens.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: monitoring-probe blind spots are adversarially exploitable, a recognized critical interpretability-for-safety pathway.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Uses pre-trained SAEs and probes, no training; guided with clear methodology.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused (map absorption blind-spot for one concept) though some construction effort.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: No-training audit on public SAEs labs have little incentive to publish; independent-friendly.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference on Gemma-2-2B with pre-trained SAEs; single mid GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Absorption is documented; its impact on safety-probe recall specifically may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Absorption is studied; tying it to safety-probe blind spots is a fresher angle.
